clue.text: Head claims underworld affected site where holidaymakers uncovered lodge

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so the first word wraps round the second

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
camp means theatrically affected or mannered

explanation.surface: A boss insists some criminal gang has damaged the lodge where tourists were found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' looks like 'discovered' but means unclothed, and 'lodge' is a verb: where holidaymakers stay naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist camp is a resort where visitors stay undressed, so it is the place uncovered holidaymakers lodge.

clue.text: Condition of prison

blocks.note: first meaning: state
second meaning: British slang for a jail or police station

explanation.surface: A complaint about the state a jail has been left in.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both for physical state, as in 'in good nick', and for a police cell or jail.

clue.text: Failure of stylish chap finishing early

indicators.note: a word that finishes early stops short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: a dude is a dandy, a man fussy about his clothes

explanation.surface: A fashionable man flops by giving up too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: DUDE loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud is something that fails to work, such as a shell that does not explode.

clue.text: Part of Austria passing close to bandit country

indicators.note: something passing goes away, so this letter departs from the word
'close to' keeps only the last letter of 'bandit'

blocks.note: Styria is one of Austria's federal states
the closing letter of bandit

explanation.surface: A traveller in Austria drives past a region known for outlaws.
explanation.walkthrough: STYRIA, the Austrian state round Graz, loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East, bordering Turkey, Iraq and Lebanon.

clue.text: Manage to take photograph in thicket

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: to cope is to manage
pic is a short informal word for a photo

explanation.surface: A nature photographer tries to get a shot while stuck in undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: A coppice is a small wood of trees cut back regularly so that dense shoots grow, a kind of thicket.

clue.text: Inappropriate time to speak on the phone with Kelvin: around Wednesday?

blocks.clueFragment: Inappropriate time to speak on the phone
blocks.note: mid-wee, while urinating, is a bad moment to take a call
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: Someone asks when it would be rude to ring, adding a name and a day.
explanation.walkthrough: The long first phrase is a cheeky cryptic description of 'mid-wee'. The question mark flags that 'around Wednesday' is only roughly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Midweek is the middle of the working week, the days centred on Wednesday.

clue.text: Upper-class person from Thailand no longer available

blocks.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
a dish that is off is no longer on the menu

explanation.surface: An aristocrat from Bangkok who has stopped being free for meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is British slang for a wealthy, well-bred person of high social class.

clue.text: Willow is more intimate, but not at first

indicators.note: not at first tells us the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: cosier means snugger, more intimate

explanation.surface: A willow tree is described as warmer and snugger, with a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: COSIER loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Fellow phoned Scotsman about penny sweet's centre being cream

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the name goes round the coin letter
the centre of a word is its middle letter, the one kept here

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
rang means telephoned
Ian is a typically Scottish first name
p is the abbreviation for a penny
the middle letter of sweet

explanation.surface: A man rings a Scot to ask about a cheap sweet with a creamy filling.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny goes inside the Scotsman's name, not inside the whole run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangipane is an almond-flavoured custard or paste used as a filling, a kind of pastry cream.

clue.text: Calculated price of houses around Kent, being spoiled

indicators.note: to house something is to give it room inside, so the region goes within

blocks.note: to cost something is to calculate its price
Kent lies in England's South East, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Someone priced up homes in the Kent area and was indulged.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, hence the compass abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper, so a cosseted person has been indulged, a synonym for spoiled.

clue.text: Sent back some discoloured ice in drink

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used
sent back means turned round to run the other way

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: discolouRED ICe

explanation.surface: A customer returns a drink because the ice in it is dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, the run of letters spells the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic drink made from fermented apple juice.

clue.text: GoPro damaged with acid in capital city

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An action camera was ruined by a chemical spill in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two parts of the fodder. A GoPro is a small action camera.
explanation.definitionFit: Podgorica is the capital and largest city of Montenegro.

clue.text: At A&E, taking drug to lower cholesterol

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the drug goes within the hospital department

blocks.note: A&E, Accident and Emergency, is a British hospital casualty department
statins are drugs prescribed to reduce blood cholesterol

explanation.surface: A patient in casualty is given cholesterol medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' looks like a preposition but is the definition: the chemical symbol. STATIN sits between A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: At is the chemical symbol for astatine, a rare radioactive halogen element.

clue.text: Banks made these cuts, losing cash ultimately

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word
'ultimately' keeps only the last letter of 'cash'

blocks.note: shaves are close cuts, as with a razor
the final letter of cash

explanation.surface: Banks made cuts and lost money in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' is not lenders but Gordon Banks, England's 1966 World Cup goalkeeper. SHAVES loses H.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalkeeper's job is stopping shots, and Gordon Banks was famous for doing this, notably against Pelé.

clue.text: Child interrupts news programme

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the following words, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: newS PROGramme

explanation.surface: A child breaks into a broadcast of the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a child or baby.

clue.text: Schedule includes match in Alabama?

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a slate is a list of planned items, a schedule
a vesta is a short wooden or wax match

explanation.surface: A sports fixture list features a game in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game, but it is the kind that is struck: VESTA. The question mark marks Alabama as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Before the Civil War, Alabama was one of the US states where slavery was legal.

clue.text: Large eggs with breakfast, lunch, and elevenses initially appealing

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the meal words

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
ova is the Latin plural for eggs
the first letters of the three meals

explanation.surface: Big eggs served at every meal of the day are tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lovable is easy to like, which is what appealing means here.

clue.text: Victor in competition with passion for drink

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word for a contest

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee
rage is a violent passion or craze

explanation.surface: The winner of a contest has a craving for alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Competition' here is the old word for a spelling contest or quilting gathering, not a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Sauce found in vessel revolting

blocks.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
up means in revolt, as in 'up in arms'

explanation.surface: Disgusting sauce discovered in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a jar or pot, but it is a boat. 'Revolting' is not disgusting but rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ketchup is a tomato sauce used as a condiment.

clue.text: Loathe taking son for expedition

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so a letter is placed within

blocks.note: to hate is to loathe
s is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent hates taking the boy on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes into HATE. 'Expedition' here is not a journey but its older sense of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed in doing something, the same as haste.

clue.text: Travel sanctions shortened carriage

indicators.note: shortened means cut down at the end, losing the final letter

blocks.note: a visa sanctions travel; the plural gives two of them

explanation.surface: Penalties on travel cut short a train service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanctions' suggests penalties but means permissions; two visas, minus the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vis-à-vis was a horse-drawn carriage in which the passengers sat facing each other.

clue.text: Cheers killed off peripheral characters in time

indicators.note: peripheral characters are the letters at the edges, the first and last

blocks.note: slain means killed
the first and last letters of time

explanation.surface: A TV show has killed minor characters in time to end the series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like the sitcom, matching the TV picture, but it is a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sláinte is the Gaelic toast meaning 'health', said when raising a glass.

clue.text: Bicycle Race is playing after Crazy

indicators.note: after says the second part comes behind the first in the answer

blocks.note: mad means crazy
a show that is on is playing

explanation.surface: The Queen song 'Bicycle Race' is playing after their track 'Crazy Little Thing'.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest Queen songs. 'Bicycle Race' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The madison is a track-cycling race in which team riders take turns, handing over with a sling.

clue.text: Improperly care for daughter with wet scrubbing cloth, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so its middle letter is kept
to scrub something is to wipe it out, so this letter is removed

blocks.note: to moisten is to wet
the central letter of cloth
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A mother neglects her girl by scrubbing her with a damp flannel.
explanation.walkthrough: MOISTEN loses O, then D is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistend is an old word for tending badly, that is, looking after something wrongly.

clue.text: Perhaps Chesterfield rector gets to date?

blocks.note: a chesterfield is a type of padded sofa
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A vicar from the town of Chesterfield finds a romantic partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesterfield looks like the Derbyshire town but is the furniture; 'date' is not romance but time.
explanation.definitionFit: So far means up to the present moment, the same as to date.

clue.text: Film following mythical boat

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A movie made after a legendary voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fargo is the 1996 Coen brothers crime movie set in Minnesota and North Dakota.

clue.text: Freed from awfully bad love triangles, at last

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled
at last points to the final letter of the word before

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of triangles

explanation.surface: Someone finally escapes a series of miserable romantic entanglements.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absolved is to be released from guilt or obligation, that is, set free.

clue.text: Bound to meet unknown Hispanic singer

blocks.note: to lope is to run with long bounding strides
z is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A fan is sure to meet an obscure Latin singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as 'certain' but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Jennifer Lopez is a singer and actor of Puerto Rican descent.

clue.text: European agreed to reveal studies

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
yes is what you say when you agree

explanation.surface: An EU official consents to publish research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' reads as a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely, so eyes means looks over or examines.

clue.text: Care! Organ replacement can lead to overbearing pomposity

indicators.note: replacement suggests putting things back in new positions, so these letters move around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that organ transplants can make a surgeon conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogance is an overbearing sense of one's own importance, a haughty self-regard.

clue.text: Source of drug, like in music

blocks.note: first meaning: the flower whose juice yields opium
second meaning: resembling the style of chart music

explanation.surface: Musicians and narcotics in one sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is the adjective formed from 'pop' plus '-py', meaning similar to that style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The opium poppy is the plant from which morphine and heroin come, and poppy also describes catchy chart-style songs.

clue.text: One's paid rugby player to scratch bottom

indicators.note: to scratch is to cancel, and the bottom of a down entry is its final letter

blocks.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

explanation.surface: A paid rugby forward caught scratching his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: PROP loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro is a professional, someone who gets wages for doing a sport or job.

clue.text: Inverted only compound containing unsaturated alcohol

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so the word reads from end to start

blocks.note: lone means sole, only

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about the sole compound with an unsaturated alcohol group.
explanation.definitionFit: An enol is an organic compound with a hydroxyl group on a carbon of a double bond, a type of unsaturated alcohol.

clue.text: New Zealand's Premier overused exercises in meeting

indicators.note: premier means first, so the opening letters of the country's two words are kept
to exercise something is to work it about, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: the initial letters of New and Zealand
taken as written

explanation.surface: The New Zealand prime minister has worn out a phrase during talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' looks like a prime minister but just means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendezvous is an arranged meeting at a set time and place.
